title: The 3pm Wall
logline: At 3pm a designer's whole afternoon turns grey and slow motion, ten minutes before the client call. One can of {product} and the colour and speed come back.

world.setting: Fieldnote Studio, a fictional small design studio in a converted brick loft in a North American city, a weekday afternoon. Long shared desks, big windows, plants, pinned-up paper mockups.
world.palette: Problem: everything desaturated to cool grey. Solution: sky blue and brushed silver from the can, warm window light, a red accent in Carmen's scarf and the pinned mockups.
fictional_brands: Fieldnote Studio (the design studio, a small line-drawn leaf mark on the glass door, added in post if legible)
Harbor and Pine (the client, shown only as abstract colour blocks on screen)
world.rules: Screens show only abstract colour blocks and blank placeholder bars. Clocks have hands and tick marks, no numerals. Every other sign, mug and notebook is blank.

locations.plate_prompt: Photoreal film still, vertical 9:16, upright vertical composition, level horizon: an empty small working design studio, well used and full of nine people's things, in a converted brick loft on a weekday afternoon, long shared wooden desks with large plain black-framed monitors on simple black stands, their backs plain matte black with no logos, showing only abstract colour blocks, big steel-framed windows, potted plants, paper mockups pinned to a cork wall as blank colour swatches, a plain round wall clock with hands and tick marks but no numbers, a small stainless office fridge in the corner. Detail is densest on the walls, shelves and back desks; the front desk stays readable. No people, no readable text, no real brands, no logos.

ingested.moment: she takes the can from the studio fridge, cracks it and drinks; colour floods out from the can

applied.moment: she applies it at the studio bathroom mirror (face mist, balm, eye cream) and colour spreads out from her fingertips

worn.moment: she puts it on at her desk (glasses, headphones, a jacket, shoes) and the colour starts from where it touches her

handheld.moment: she picks it up from her desk drawer (a stylus, a mouse, earbuds, a tool) and the first click brings the colour back

carried.moment: she unzips it from under her desk (a bag, a case, an organiser) and colour pours out of it

home.moment: it sits in her corner of the studio (a chair, a lamp, a desk riser, a plant light) and switching it on turns the corner back to colour

consumable.moment: she tears open the refill or pack from the studio kitchen and colour spreads from the pack

product_adjacent_props.moment: the fridge shelf around the product and the spot on her desk where it lands are generic; the swatch deck, clock, bell and pothos belong to the studio and stay

beats.summary: Carmen at her desk, the whole studio drained to grey, the clock at three. She names the pain to camera.
Slow motion: her cursor crawls, a sheet of paper hangs mid-fall, a coworker yawns forever. Walt reminds her the client call is in ten minutes.
She opens the grey studio fridge; the can is the only thing in full colour. She cracks it and colour spreads from the can up her arm.
Colour and normal speed are back. She says the product line, then works fast: mockups snap together on screen.
Walt watches her present and approves in two words. A top and bottom split shows 3pm Carmen against 3:10pm Carmen.
The can on her desk in warm afternoon light, tagline.

lore: Fieldnote Studio is nine people on the fourth floor of a 1911 button factory in Pittsburgh. The freight elevator still has its brass scissor gate and still gets stuck between floors.

Walt Brennan founded the studio in 1998 on the same oak drafting table he works at now. He rings a small brass counter bell on the shelf every time a client signs off, and it has not rung since August.
Carmen Reyes has been there six years. At 3:10pm she presents the rebrand for Harbor and Pine, a family seafood grocer with 14 stores and the studio's biggest account.
The studio fridge carries a hand-drawn tally of lost afternoons in grey marker: little sleeping faces, 23 of them this quarter.
The trailing pothos on Carmen's monitor was rescued from the lobby bin in her first week and now reaches the floor.

world_bible.wear_and_time: A Tuesday in late October, 3:00pm to 3:12pm. Overcast in the grey world, then low gold sun breaking through the factory windows once colour returns. The coffee has gone cold with a skin on it, the pothos needs water, sticky notes have multiplied round her monitor, the cork wall is three rounds of revisions deep, the bell is dusty from two quiet months, and the fridge tally is one face away from a new row.

the stylus scratching slowly, then fast
the fridge seal unsticking and the compressor hum
the ring tab cracking with a fine hiss
the freight elevator gate clanking somewhere below
one bright ding of the brass bell
